title: Establish the first Craft Product Feature inside its Product context
outcome: Establish one owner-reviewable System Construction Product Feature thesis contextualized by the Craft Product, aligned to CAV2-D20 Craft Method, preserving same-lineage continuity from the former DomainSpec v2 name, and exposing the definition, ontology, architecture, migration, and evidence decisions that must precede implementation changes.
rationale: Selecting Craft as DomainSpec v2's new name does not move source, implementation, consumers, or authority. The Craft Project must define the first Product Feature inside the Product context, bind it to the Method without collapsing their identities, and preserve exact lineage and migration evidence before legacy paths change.
scope: one CAV2-D60 Craft Project and one linked CAV2-D59 Goal
a project-local System Construction Product Feature identity and thesis candidate
the Craft Product Thesis as immediate Product context and the CyberAlchemy Product Thesis as parent context
CAV2-D20 Craft Method as the system-building method
same-Product-lineage rename continuity from DomainSpec v2 to Craft
typed residue for physical and authority migration still pending
open gates for terminology, ontology, architecture, first slice, migration, and evidence
exclusions: collapsing Product, Project, Method, Product Feature, or Product Capability
unproved physical path, consumer, import, or authority migration
architecture selection, implementation, publication, release, deployment, or external effects
owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Craft Project owner plus DomainSpec v2 owner for inherited meaning

success_conditions.statement: Craft has one schema-valid Project and one linked Goal that trace to the parent CyberAlchemy Product Thesis while coordinating the separate Craft Product.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The Project and Goal close bidirectionally, use CA2-PROJECT-CRAFT, cite CA2-THESIS-GOVERNED-HMI, identify CA2-PRODUCT-CRAFT and CAV2-D20 in the local identity graph, and retain authority_effect none.

success_conditions.statement: The Craft Product Feature thesis is reviewed and its commitment posture is explicitly decided by the product owner.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: An exact owner decision over the candidate thesis digest that either commits, revises, or rejects it without implying implementation authority.

success_conditions.statement: Product Feature meaning and its relationship to Product context are defined and admitted in the product ontology.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A canonical definition decision plus an ontology relation that keeps Product, Product Feature, Project, Goal, and Product Capability distinct.

success_conditions.statement: The first bounded Craft feature slice and its exact DomainSpec inheritance boundary are selected.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: An owner-selected slice with dependency-closed source inventory, preserved behavior, architecture obligations, conformance boundary, and runtime evidence target.

evidence_requirements: Project, Product context, Product Feature, Goal, Product Capability, public craft capability, and .craft state must remain separate identities.
The candidate thesis must be reviewed by exact digest before its commitment state changes.
DomainSpec succession must remain an intended direction until an exact adoption decision transfers responsibility.
Static conformance, runtime evidence, and owner adoption must remain separate claims.

revision_history.change: Created the Craft Project and first Product Feature thesis; established the separate Product, Project, and Method identities.
Recorded Craft as the new name of the DomainSpec v2 Product lineage and kept physical and authority migration explicitly open.
revision_history.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Craft Project owner

challenge_route: Challenge Product meaning through the Craft Product owner, Project coordination through the Craft Project owner, Method meaning through definitions-governance, inherited DomainSpec meaning through the DomainSpec v2 owner, and future architecture or implementation claims through their separately named owners.
